Executive Overview

A Digital Learning Partnership Proposal for Maharashtra

A proposed school-focused learning initiative for discussion with the Government of Maharashtra.

TELEDU
Value Your Time

TELEDU (Teledu Private Limited) runs teledu.in, an online learning platform with courses for Classes 6–12 and preparation courses for JEE and NEET. Its courses currently follow CBSE/ICSE. This proposal asks how the platform could be adapted, tested and evaluated for students in Maharashtra.

Purpose of this meeting

To introduce TELEDU, demonstrate the existing platform, and seek the Department's guidance on whether — and how — a small, evaluated pilot for Maharashtra's students could be considered.

Programme objectives

What the proposed initiative would aim to do.

Proposed
  • Offer students additional practice, revision and chapter-wise assessment that complements classroom teaching.
  • Develop Marathi-medium and Maharashtra State Board-aligned content, subject to academic review.
  • Give parents and schools clear, aggregated progress information.
  • Test the approach in a small, measurable pilot before any wider decision.
  • Explore a transparent student scholarship or fee-support mechanism, only through an authorised route.
  • Report results honestly to the Department, whatever they show.

What this means for a digital programme

Connectivity varies

Roughly 28% of schools report no internet facility, so any programme needs low-bandwidth and offline-friendly options.

Language & curriculum

Many students learn in Marathi under the State Board; CBSE/ICSE content alone would not meet their needs.

Urban, rural & underserved

The pilot should include rural, tribal and aspirational-district schools, not only well-connected urban ones.

How TELEDU could support participating students

A complement to classroom teaching — not a replacement for teachers or the school's curriculum.

Relevant digital content

Lessons matched to the student's class and board.

Maths & Science support

Concept explanations and worked examples.

Chapter-wise assessments

Practice & revision

Question sets for revision before tests and exams.

Progress tracking

Parent summaries

How this information would be used

Aggregated answers would help TELEDU decide which Marathi content to build first, which subjects need the most support, whether offline or low-data options are needed, and where teachers may need help.

Privacy safeguards

  • Collect only what the programme needs; no unnecessary personal details.
  • Student-level collection only with appropriate notice and verifiable parental consent or other lawful authorisation, as required under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.
  • Access controls and a defined retention period.
  • Only aggregated results shown to the Department; no identifiable answers.

A small, measurable pilot

A proposal for discussion — not an approved rollout. Schools, classes and timing would be agreed with the Department.

Pilot objectives

  • Measure change in chapter-test performance
  • Test Marathi content with real students
  • Learn what schools, teachers and parents need

TELEDU would support an online assessment through InTest, subject to confirmation of the platform's official name, its technical suitability and acceptance by the relevant authority.

Proposed Assessment Service — Subject to Approval by the Relevant Authority

Why the assessment is needed

The mandatory requirement, as publicly reported.

As reported · Gazette to be verified

The requirement

"Working knowledge of Marathi language"

Maharashtra amended its motor vehicle rules in August 2026 to make a working knowledge of Marathi mandatory for taxi and autorickshaw drivers. Transport officials say it is needed to communicate with passengers.

Aug 2026Maharashtra Motor Vehicles (Third Amendment) Rules, 2026 notified, amending Rules 4(4) and 78 of the Maharashtra Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989
Mid-Aug 2026RTO teams began checking drivers' Marathi
29 Aug 2026State told the Bombay High Court that drivers have been given one more year to learn Marathi

TELEDU / InTest authorised to testNot authorised
Where TELEDU could help: the one-year extension gives drivers time to learn. TELEDU proposes to help them learn (Marathi courses), practise (practice tests) and, only if the relevant authority accepts it, be assessed online.

Automated Scholarship Selection

Selecting scholarship candidates by test performance and completion time

TELEDU's proposed automated process for identifying students for scholarship support. This is not an approved government scholarship programme; final awards would follow the approved policy and funding arrangements.

Approval status

Current stage: Proposed
  1. ProposedFor discussion

Not yet confirmed

The system identifies and ranks candidates; it does not award scholarships. Awards would follow the final approved policy, the confirmed funding arrangements and verification of each candidate.

Selection flow

Seven steps from test to award. Click any step for details.

Proposed
Step 1 of 7

How the ranking works

Score and completion time are both recorded and combined by a predefined, published rule.

Formula to be finalised

Selection logic

1 · Eligibility checkConditions to be finalised

Only students meeting the approved eligibility conditions are ranked.

2 · Assessment scoreRecorded

Each student's test score is recorded automatically.

3 · Completion timeRecorded

Time taken, within the same fixed time limit for everyone, is recorded automatically.

4 · Predefined ruleTo be finalised

Score and time are combined by one published rule, fixed before any test begins and applied identically to all.

Recommended safeguards for the rule

  • Academic performance stays the main factor; completion time should not outweigh a clearly higher score
  • Same test difficulty and the same time limit for every candidate
  • Approved accessibility accommodations carry no time penalty
  • Rule, weights and tie-breaks published before assessments begin and not changed afterwards
  • Results shown with anonymised IDs; no personal information displayed publicly
